answer: Each agent identity must lock a refundable stake before it can join the transaction thread; peers randomly challenge its signed claims, and a quorum can slash the stake when two identities collude or contradict an audited record. A sybil operator therefore has to fund every fake identity and risk losing that capital, while honest agents recover their deposits. A marble-sized claim still carries a verifiable history in the shared kernel, so multiplying names does not multiply trust.
